q.t: How many factors does 12 have?
q.k: len([d for d in range(1,13) if 12%d==0])
q.e: Factors come in pairs that multiply to 12: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4. That gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.

q.t: What is the third multiple of 7?
q.e: Multiples are the times table: 7, 14, 21 …

q.t: Is 17 a prime number?
o: Yes — its only factors are 1 and 17
q.e: A prime has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. Nothing else divides 17.

q.t: What is the smallest prime number?
q.e: 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime. 2 has exactly two: 1 and 2.

q.t: Find the HCF of 6 and 9.
q.k: math.gcd(6,9)
q.e: Factors of 6: 1, 2, 3, 6. Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9. The highest one they share is 3.

q.t: Find the LCM of 4 and 6.
q.e: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12 … Multiples of 6: 6, 12 … The first one they share is 12.

q.t: The number 1 is:
q.e: A prime needs exactly two factors and a composite more than two. 1 has only one factor.

q.t: Which of these is divisible by 2?
q.e: A number is divisible by 2 when its last digit is even.

q.t: Which is the only even prime number?
q.e: Every other even number has 2 as an extra factor, so it cannot be prime.

q.t: How many factors does a prime number have?
q.e: Exactly two — 1 and the number itself. That is the definition of prime.

q.t: Find the HCF of 36 and 48.
q.k: math.gcd(36,48)
q.e: 36 = 2² × 3² and 48 = 2⁴ × 3. Take the common primes with the smaller powers: 2² × 3 = 12.

q.t: Find the LCM of 12 and 18.
q.e: 12 = 2² × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3². Take every prime with the larger power: 2² × 3² = 36.

q.t: Write the prime factorisation of 60.
q.e: Keep splitting until every factor is prime: 60 = 2 × 30 = 2 × 2 × 15 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5.

q.t: Is 2,358 divisible by 9?
o: Yes — the digits add up to 18
No — the digits add up to 18
q.e: A number is divisible by 9 when its digit sum is: 2 + 3 + 5 + 8 = 18.

q.t: How many prime numbers are there between 20 and 30?
q.k: len([n for n in range(21,30) if all(n%d for d in range(2,n))])
q.e: Only 23 and 29. The others are even, or divisible by 3 or 5.

q.t: Which pair are twin primes?
q.e: Twin primes are two primes that differ by exactly 2.

q.t: Which pair of numbers is co-prime?
q.e: Co-prime numbers share no factor except 1. 8 = 2 × 2 × 2 and 15 = 3 × 5 have nothing in common.

q.t: Find the LCM of 5 and 8.
q.e: They are co-prime, so the LCM is simply their product.

q.t: What is the HCF of any two co-prime numbers?
q.e: Co-prime means the only common factor is 1.

q.t: Is 1331 divisible by 11?
q.e: Add alternate digits: 1 + 3 = 4 and 3 + 1 = 4. The difference is 0, so 11 divides it (1331 = 11 × 121).

q.t: The HCF of two numbers is 6 and their LCM is 72. One number is 18. Find the other.
q.e: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers. 6 × 72 = 432, and 432 ÷ 18 = 24.

q.t: Find the greatest number that divides 43, 91 and 183 leaving the same remainder each time.
q.e: If the remainders are equal, the number divides the differences 48, 92 and 140. Their HCF is 4.

q.t: Three bells ring every 6, 8 and 12 minutes. They ring together now. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
q.e: The time must be a multiple of all three: LCM of 6, 8, 12 = 24.

q.t: Find the least number which leaves remainder 7 when divided by 12, 16 and 24.
q.e: LCM of 12, 16, 24 is 48 — the smallest number all three divide exactly. Add the remainder: 55.

q.t: Find the greatest number that divides 245 and 1029 leaving remainder 5 each time.
q.e: Take the remainder away first: it must divide 240 and 1024 exactly. HCF(240, 1024) = 16.

q.t: Find the LCM of 15, 20 and 30.
A floor is 4 m 20 cm by 3 m 60 cm. What is the side of the largest square tile that covers it exactly (in cm)?
q.k: math.gcd(420,360)
q.e: The tile’s side must divide both 420 cm and 360 cm. The largest such number is their HCF, 60.

q.t: Find the smallest 4-digit number divisible by 18, 24 and 32.
q.k: min(n for n in range(1000,2000) if n%18==0 and n%24==0 and n%32==0)
q.e: LCM = 288. Its multiples: 288, 576, 864, 1152 — the first with 4 digits.

q.t: How many prime numbers are less than 50?
q.k: len([n for n in range(2,50) if all(n%d for d in range(2,n))])

q.t: 43* is divisible by 6. What is the smallest digit that can replace *?
q.k: min(x for x in range(10) if (430+x)%6==0)
q.e: Divisible by 6 means divisible by 2 (even last digit) and by 3 (digit sum 7 + * a multiple of 3). * = 2 gives 432.

q.t: What is the least number that must be subtracted from 1000 to get a number divisible by 15, 18 and 24?
q.e: LCM of 15, 18, 24 is 360. The largest multiple below 1000 is 720, so subtract 280.

q.t: Find the largest 3-digit number exactly divisible by 6, 8 and 12.
q.k: max(n for n in range(100,1000) if n%24==0)
q.e: LCM = 24. 999 ÷ 24 leaves remainder 15, so 999 − 15 = 984.

q.t: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4 and their HCF is 5. Find their LCM.
q.e: The numbers are 3 × 5 = 15 and 4 × 5 = 20. LCM of 15 and 20 = 60.

q.t: Three traffic lights change every 48, 72 and 108 seconds. They change together at 7:00:00. After how many seconds do they next change together?
q.k: min(n for n in range(1,2000) if n%48==0 and n%72==0 and n%108==0)
q.e: LCM of 48, 72, 108 = 432 seconds (7 minutes 12 seconds).

q.t: The product of two numbers is 2160 and their HCF is 12. Find their LCM.
q.e: HCF × LCM = product, so LCM = 2160 ÷ 12 = 180.

q.t: What is the HCF of any two consecutive even numbers?
q.k: math.gcd(14,16)
q.e: Both are divisible by 2. They differ by only 2, so no bigger number can divide both.

q.t: How many factors does 72 have?
q.k: len([d for d in range(1,73) if 72%d==0])
q.e: 72 = 2³ × 3². A factor may use 0–3 twos (4 choices) and 0–2 threes (3 choices): 4 × 3 = 12.

q.t: Find the least number which leaves remainders 4, 5 and 6 when divided by 6, 7 and 8.
q.k: min(n for n in range(1,1000) if n%6==4 and n%7==5 and n%8==6)
q.e: Each time the number is 2 short of a multiple (6 − 4 = 7 − 5 = 8 − 6 = 2). So it is LCM − 2 = 168 − 2 = 166.

q.t: Find the sum of all the prime numbers between 1 and 20.
q.k: sum(n for n in range(2,20) if all(n%d for d in range(2,n)))

q.t: Find the greatest 4-digit number divisible by 12, 15 and 20.
q.k: max(n for n in range(1000,10000) if n%60==0)
q.e: LCM = 60. 9999 ÷ 60 leaves remainder 39, so 9999 − 39 = 9960.
